The work on the ground

Gospel proclamation that leads somewhere.

Jesus Christ remains at the center. Campaigns are prepared with local pastors, followed by discipleship, and connected to the long work of healthy local churches.

01

Mass evangelism

Five-day Gospel campaigns bring a clear proclamation of Jesus beyond church walls. Local congregations help prepare, host and follow up with those who respond.

Campaigns on the Swedish site
02

Church planting

Joshua Campaign works with Ethiopian leaders to establish congregations where the Gospel has not had a strong presence—building local capacity beyond the event.

Church planting work
03

Pioneer mission

Mission aviation and field teams extend access to remote communities, supporting missionaries, medical response and practical connection where roads cannot.

Mission Institute
Campaigns

Wednesday through Sunday. Local pastors prepare the ground, teams proclaim Jesus, and follow-up material connects new believers with churches.

The Swedish ministry site budgets approximately SEK 250,000 for a five-day campaign. Each event is built through partnership rather than parachute ministry.

Planting

Since 2007, the work has grown through a close relationship with pioneer pastor Belay Kekeba. A new Ethiopian denomination was formed with a six-person church-planting core team in 2015.

Pastor Mohammed Seid Ali leads daily work in eastern Ethiopia with vice director Zekarias Kitaba. A pioneer pastor can be supported through the Swedish office at SEK 600 per month for two years.

Mission aviation

The Mission Institute uses helicopter access to move missionaries and medical teams toward remote communities.

Flights also support evacuation, food and medicine supply, vaccination work and service requested by local authorities.

Follow-up

Joshua Campaign reports distributing more than 3.8 million salvation and follow-up books through its history.

The measure is not simply a gathered crowd, but people welcomed into local discipleship and congregations.

“The mission is to take the Gospel to the most remote places on earth.”
Joshua Campaign vision
Leader & featured evangelist

Per Åkvist

Per Åkvist leads Joshua Campaign Ethiopia. Together with his wife Abbi, he has carried responsibility for the work in Ethiopia and the Sweden office since 2007. Before that, Per spent fourteen years planting churches across the former Soviet Union; the Åkvists began serving in Ethiopia in 2005 and then joined Joshua Campaign. Abbi was born in Ethiopia and raised in Sweden, bringing a deeply personal bridge between the two countries.

“A human right for every person to hear the Gospel at least once in their lifetime.”

Per’s leadership keeps Joshua Campaign close to the local church: campaigns mobilize pastors, new believers are connected for follow-up, and pioneer leaders are equipped for sustained ministry.

Hear Per speak about Joshua Campaign
Co-founder · Founding vision

Karl Härgestam

Karl and Jennifer Härgestam co-founded Joshua Campaign International. Karl left Sweden at 21 with a mandate to take the Gospel to unreached peoples in Africa, helping establish a movement marked by pioneer evangelism, large-scale outreach, aviation and church planting.

Today Karl serves as Global Missions Director for the Pentecostal Church of God. His enduring message—One Chance for Every Person—connects the founding impulse of Joshua Campaign with a wider global call to ensure no person is overlooked.

Distinct identity. Shared assignment.

Joshua Campaign keeps its own story, leadership and field identity while standing in clear alignment with the One Chance conviction: every person has a birthright to hear the Gospel at least once. Operation 326 puts that conviction to work by identifying frontier gaps and helping prayer, pioneers and resources move toward them.

The connections shown here are shared mission and public ministry relationships. They do not imply that these distinct ministries are legally controlled by Joshua Campaign.

The Joshua Campaign way

Keep the roots. Strengthen the reach.

The identity remains the one established on the Swedish site: mass evangelism, church mobilization and mission networks. The 2026 expression makes the alignment clearer without replacing the relationships and field leadership that have carried the work.

“Go through the camp and tell the people, ‘Get your provisions ready. Three days from now you will cross the Jordan here to go in and take possession of the land the Lord your God is giving you for your own.’” — Joshua 1:11

Campaigns are not the finish line. They serve the local church’s long obedience—disciples formed, leaders raised and congregations planted where the Gospel needs a durable home.
